title: US National Debt Crosses $40 Trillion For First Time, Rising By $1 Trillion In Just Five Months
text:
World
Swarajya Staff
Aug 20, 2026 | Updated 09:36 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!

The United States crossed a historic fiscal milestone this week as the national debt surpassed $40 trillion for the first time.
The total reached $40.05 trillion on Tuesday (18 August), just four and a half years after topping $30 trillion, marking an acceleration in borrowing that has alarmed fiscal watchdogs and economists alike.
The unprecedented figure represents an increase of $1 trillion in just five months, far outpacing earlier projections.
A decade ago, the national debt level stood at $19.4 trillion, meaning America's borrowing has more than doubled in less than 10 years.
The federal government now borrows $6 billion per day, over half of which goes towards interest on existing debt—more than the entire national defence budget.
Rising interest costs have become the second-largest budget expenditure.
Interest on the debt has totalled nearly $1.2 trillion this year and is the largest budget item outside of Social Security and Medicare.
Years of escalating budget deficits, pushed higher by stimulus funding during the Covid pandemic, have seen the public share of debt near 100 per cent of gross domestic product.
The Treasury Department reported the milestone arrived months earlier than anticipated, partly due to billions in lost revenue from invalidated tariffs.
Treasury reported a $432.3 billion deficit in July, the highest monthly total since March 2021, with the year-to-date shortfall nearing $1.8 trillion, higher than the same period last year.
The rapid accumulation has raised concerns about long-term fiscal sustainability.
Since Trump took office a second time in January 2025, the US debt load has increased by $3.8 trillion, for total growth of $11.6 trillion across his two terms.
Budget analysts warn that borrowing could hit the $41.1 trillion debt ceiling by early next year, forcing lawmakers to either suspend it or raise it again to avoid default.
